newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls confidence vote on immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls confidence vote on immigrants.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government called a confidence vote in the Senate (upper house) on Wednesday to help push through a draft law on immigration.

Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano told the assembly the cabinet was requesting the vote after hard-right and other opponents of the bill submitted some 7,000 amendments. Victory on the confidence motion would sweep the amendments away.

Parliamentary party leaders in the Senate were expected to meet to decide when to hold the vote. Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition has a majority in the upper house, making victory on the motion likely.

The draft law is designed to regularise the status of thousands of illegal immigrants who have registered with police to remain in Italy under the terms of a partial amnesty contained in past stop-gap legislation known as decrees.
The latest of the decrees expired earlier this month at the end of its 60-day life.

Past governments routinely re-issued expired decrees but the Constitutional Court recently banned the practice. The ruling has forced Prodi's government to resort to a string of confidence votes to get pending legislation passed.
